newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Nov platinum imports seen continuing fall.
newsitem.headline: Japan Nov platinum imports seen continuing fall.

text.p: A plunge in demand from investors is likely to pressure Japan's platinum imports in November, continuing a drop registered in October, traders said.
They also said palladium imports in November will be a touch lower than the same month last year, as demand from electrical firms has stayed lacklustre.

"Japan's platinum imports in November could be around five tonnes, weighed down by sharp declines in investment demand, while palladium imports are estimated at around six tonnes," an official of a major bullion house said.
Platinum imports in November last year were 5.93 tonnes and those of palladium 6.636 tonnes, Finance Ministry data showed.
Platinum imports in October were down 28.8 percent from the same month a year earlier at 5.28 tonnes, while palladium imports fell 26.9 percent from October 1995.
Platinum demand from investors for 1996 was likely to be around four tonnes, half that of last year, hit by a rise in yen-based retail prices reflecting the yen's weaker tone, the official said.
The traders expect platinum demand for the year from jewellery firms to be at least steady after enjoying record demand of 46 tonnes in 1995.
Cumulative imports in the first 10 months of 1996 for platinum were down 4.5 percent at 57.48 tonnes, and those for palladium were down 22.1 percent to 66.26 tonnes, the ministry data showed.
